Subject: Light Up a Life 2026

A little note about our Light Up a Life tree, which will be in the shop window from Saturday 21 November.

Memory tags will be available at the counter from Monday 16 November. You can write a name here in the shop, or take an envelope home and write your tag there if you prefer. The suggested donation is £3, but the tree is for everyone who wants to remember someone. You are very welcome to add a name in whatever way feels right for you.

On Saturday 28 November at 4pm, we’ll switch on the lights together. The Gildencroft Primary choir will be back to sing a few carols, and Doreen is bringing her mince pies again. All the names on the tags will be read at the hospice remembrance service on Sunday 13 December at 3pm, in the day centre. You don’t have to attend the service for a name to be read.

Hilary asked whether we were doing the tree again this year. We are, Hilary, and you and your sister would be very welcome. I remember you saying that having your mum’s name on the tree last year meant so much to you. Thank you for telling us.

The tree is for anyone who is grieving, not only hospice families. And you don’t need to write a tag or buy anything to come by. If you’d simply like a quiet moment, you can come in and stand beside the tree. You are welcome here.

It’s seven years this month since my husband, Ray, died at the hospice. The first year I hung his tag, I could hardly write his name. These days I write it at the counter, with the same pen. I don’t say that to make this about me, but because I know that remembering can feel different from one year to the next. There’s no right way to do it, and no timetable for grief.

Thank you to everyone who added a name, came to stand with us, sang along, or helped make last year’s tree feel so full of care. It meant a great deal to see people remembering together. We hope you’ll join us again this year, in whatever way feels right for you.

Jean and everyone at Wensum Valley Hospice Bookshop
